Fiberglass and gelcoat repair: cracks, chips, blisters, transom and stringer work

Dock rash, a cracked chine, spider cracks on the deck, a soft transom. Fiberglass specialists repair it structurally and color-match the gelcoat so it disappears.

When
Any crack that holds water, soft spots underfoot, blisters at haul-out, after an impact.
Time on site
Half a day to several days depending on scope
What it usually costs here
$250 to $900 for cosmetic repairs; structural transom and stringer work $2,000 and up, quoted after inspection.

What's included

  • Gelcoat chip and crack repair with color match
  • Impact and dock-rash repair
  • Blister repair below the waterline
  • Transom and stringer repair and replacement
  • Deck soft-spot repair
  • Through-hull and hardware rebedding

In Tampa Bay specifically

Oyster bars and the concrete seawalls of Pinellas canals account for most of the chine and keel damage mechanics see.

Questions we get

Can you match an older boat's faded color?

Yes. The repair is tinted to the current color, not the factory color, so it blends.

Is a soft transom urgent?

Yes if an outboard hangs on it. It is a safety issue, not a cosmetic one.
